column3: The Greek says tongues appeared to them and then uses singular “it sat”; BSB makes the tongues the subject throughout.
“Native language” renders the image of the language in which they were born.
The Greek says they are “filled with” sweet wine, rather than explicitly drunk.
“The crowd” makes the Greek pronoun explicit.
The Greek says “of My Spirit” and uses the image “all flesh,” rendered as “My Spirit” and “all people.”
The Greek explicitly says “of My Spirit.”
“Billows” renders the Greek image of vapor or mist of smoke.
The Greek begins an extended accusative construction naming Jesus rather than explicitly “Jesus … was.”
“From the dead” and “clutches” are supplied; the Greek speaks of loosing the birth pains of death.
The first two Greek verbs are past, rather than present; σάρξ is “flesh,” rendered as “body.”
The Greek address includes “men” as well as “brothers.”
“One of his descendants” supplies the unstated object after the Greek “from the fruit of his loins.”
